records.headline: Sir Patrick Stewart, Star Trek and X-Men actor, dies at 86
records.text: Patrick Stewart, the British actor best known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, died Wednesday at 86 after a brief illness. Born in Yorkshire in 1940, he began his career with Britain's Royal Shakespeare Company and National Theatre before moving to Hollywood. He won two Olivier awards for stage work and a Grammy for narration, and was nominated for four Emmys.

records.headline: Binance freezes billions after suspected $6.3 billion security breach
records.text: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer allowed hackers to steal an estimated $6.3 billion. Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze $1.57 billion and $800 million respectively in linked assets. Bitcoin dropped more than 3% to a six-week low, and Coinbase Global shares fell 4.8%, but analysts said the market appeared confident Binance had enough financial resources to cover user losses.

records.headline: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde steps down nine months early
records.text: Christine Lagarde announced she is stepping down as European Central Bank president nine months early, effective February 2027, to gain freedom to speak publicly on broader issues. She said ECB rules of neutrality prevented her from engaging in important debates about economic matters and truth. Her early departure triggers a succession race to lead the eurozone's central bank during a period of weak growth and inflation of 3.8 percent.

records.headline: Israeli election produces no clear winner as Arab parties make historic gains
records.text: Israel's election produced no clear winner as Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition and the opposition both fell short of the 61 seats needed to govern. Arab-led parties made historic gains, winning 19 seats, prompting Netanyahu to claim foreign interference; Qatar denied the accusations and election officials found no evidence of systematic violations. President Herzog will consult with party leaders and choose a candidate to attempt forming a government.

records.headline: Australian court orders Erin Patterson never be released from prison for mushroom poisonings
records.text: Victoria's Court of Appeal ordered Erin Patterson to never be released from prison for poisoning her estranged husband's family members with death cap mushrooms at a lunch she hosted in July 2023. The court found the crimes involved careful planning and calculated deception, and that a 33-year non-parole term failed to reflect the calculated criminality. Patterson can apply to Australia's High Court for a final appeal.

records.headline: Hong Kong leader apologises for government failures in residential fire that killed 168 people
records.text: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee apologised for government failures that contributed to a November 2025 fire at Wang Fuk Court housing complex that killed 168 people. An independent investigation found decades of regulatory failure and "lax enforcement" by four government departments. Housing Secretary Winnie Ho resigned, and authorities charged seven individuals and two companies with offences including manslaughter, though some victims' families said political accountability fell short.

records.headline: Russian drone strike on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14 people
records.text: A Russian jet-powered drone struck a crowded platform at Dnipro's main railway station Thursday, killing at least 14 people and wounding at least 14 others including an 11-year-old. Separate Russian attacks killed two teenage girls in Chernihiv and three civilians in Kremenchuk. The strikes continued despite a localised ceasefire in the southern city of Oleshky credited by both sides to US first lady Melania Trump's involvement.

records.headline: China expels record 33 members from Communist Party amid intensified purges under Xi
records.text: China expelled a record 33 members from the Communist Party at its fifth plenum this week, amid intensified purges under Xi Jinping. Only 279 of 376 Central Committee members originally named in 2022 attended the gathering, the highest number of absences in modern Chinese history. Xi has removed so many high-ranking officials—51 in his current term alone—that observers worry there are few suitable candidates to fill vacancies ahead of the party congress expected in late 2027.

beats.evidence: Only 279 of 376 Central Committee members originally named in 2022 attended the gathering, the highest number of absences in modern Chinese history.
beats.action: A grid pattern showing 376 positions fills partially—279 positions glow while 97 positions dim and fade, illustrating the absence of Central Committee members at the gathering

beats.evidence: Xi has removed so many high-ranking officials—51 in his current term alone—that observers worry there are few suitable candidates to fill vacancies ahead of the party congress expected in late 2027.
beats.action: Empty rectangular frames accumulate on the left side of the composition (representing 51 vacancies from current term), while a smaller pool of remaining candidate shapes on the right appears visibly constrained in size

previousIssues: Beat 1 / group g1 draws exactly 5 rectangular shapes departing from the circle, but the storyboard action description says '33 shapes visibly departing.' The drawing therefore implies a specific small count (5) of expelled members. Under the audit rules, a small representative group is acceptable as a symbol—HOWEVER, the board description itself explicitly states '33 shapes visibly departing from the top edge,' making the drawn count of 5 a concrete mismatch with the board's own stated quantitative representation. More critically, 5 visible departure shapes could be read as asserting that only 5 members were expelled, contradicting source 0's reported figure of 33.
